sources.citation: Ramírez Lajara, Francisco G. 2017. A Brief Description of the Noun Phrase Structure in Apoala Mixtec. Working paper/Ms., San José State University (ResearchGate; from the CoLang 2014 Apoala Mixtec practicum).
sources.note: Only known modern linguistic description of Apoala Mixtec by a linguist; a 'brief description' likely opens with transcription conventions (tone, possibly stress on the couplet).

sources.citation: Auderset, Sandra. 2025. Mixtec Sound Change Database 2.0: Integrating Tone Change. Journal of Open Humanities Data 11: 37, 1-6. doi:10.5334/johd.322 (+ MixteCaSo GitHub data/, main branch, checked 2026-09-20).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: p. 2-3 'Sampling strategy': tone module restricted to varieties 'for which tonal contrasts were marked systematically and in a reliable way' (46 of 105; 43 coded). Apoala/Apazco are not among them; their 249 rows in source josserand1983mixtec) have no tone notation. Confirms that as of 2025 the comparative Mixtecanist literature has no tone-marked data, let alone a prosodic description, for this languoid.

sources.citation: Auderset, Sandra & Eric W. Campbell. 2024. A Mixtec Sound Change Database. Journal of Open Humanities Data 10:24, 1-13 (+ MixteCaSo/MixteCoDB and sources.bib from GitHub).
sources.note: No stress statement. Metadata show that for Santiago Apoala, Santa María Apazco, San Miguel Chicahua, San Pedro Jocotipac and Santiago Ixtaltepec the only data source is Josserand 1983 wordlists; Apoala is absent from the 42-variety tone module — i.e. the compilers know of no tone/prosody description for this language.

sources.citation: Swanton, Michael W. 2024. Mesoamerican mantic names as an etymological source of Mixtec vocabulary. Ancient Mesoamerica 35: 619-644.
sources.note: No stress statement. Cites tone-marked Apoala Mixtec forms (tétà 'opossum', ðúʔũ̀, kònèhú, ʧékà) from p.c. José Carlos Jiménez Hernández (San Antonio Nduayaco, Apoala) and discusses Apoala vowel history (*e > a; sources of long /ee/); general Mixtec remark that unfooted (pre-couplet) syllables show fewer tone/nasal oppositions.

sources.citation: Auderset, Sandra, Simon J. Greenhill, Christian T. DiCanio & Eric W. Campbell. 2023. Subgrouping in a 'dialect continuum': A Bayesian phylogenetic analysis of the Mixtecan language family. Journal of Language Evolution 8(1): 33-63.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; classification only (Apoala 'a very conservative Mixtec variety'; Apoala and Apazco as distinct as separate languages). Apoala data = Josserand 1983.

sources.citation: Valiñas, Leopoldo. 2019. 'Mixteco de la región nororiental', Enciclopedia de la Literatura en México (elem.mx/lenguas/datos/237).
sources.note: Sociolinguistic/variant overview only (INALI 'mixteco del noreste' = da'an davi: Coixtlahuaca, Chicahua, Huautla, Apazco, Apoala); nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: López García, Ubaldo. 2008. Sa'vi, el lenguaje ceremonial. In M. Jansen & L. van Broekhoven (eds.), Mixtec Writing and Society / Escritura de Ñuu Dzaui, pp. 407ff. Amsterdam: KNAW Press.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Fn. 1 p. 407: to'on 'palabra' vs to'on (tono bajo) 'arranca' vs tó'on (tono alto) 'arrancó' — tone is lexical/grammatical. P. 407: 'nuestra lengua ha sido y es oral y.. a la fecha no existe un análisis detallado' — i.e. no detailed linguistic analysis of Apoala Mixtec existed as of 2008. Table 1 (p. 409) gives the Apoala pronoun system.

sources.citation: López García, Ubaldo. 2007. Sa'vi: Discursos ceremoniales de Yutsa To'on (Apoala). PhD dissertation, Universiteit Leiden. Capítulo I 'La Literatura Oral de Ñuu Savi' (pp. 9-26) + title/índice/introducción + 'Vocabulario esencial' (pp. 293-298).
sources.note: Nothing on stress/acento. Native-speaker author states (fn. 2, p. 23) that Mixtec is a tonal language and gives an Apoala minimal triplet ñu'u 'tierra' (tono medio) / ñu'u 'lumbre' (tono bajo on last u) / ñú'u 'Dios' (tono alto on first u). Orthography follows the Ve'e Tu'un Savi practical alphabet (p. 10); vocabulary is written without systematic tone or stress marks.

sources.citation: García Santiago, Mijail (asesora lingüística: Inga McKendry). 1999. Na kavi ndo na daa ku kiti tata ndo. Lección 3: Los animales domésticos, sonidos de la combinación nd. Mixteco de Santiago Apoala, Nochixtlán, Oaxaca. Versión preliminar, diciembre de 1999 (25 ejemplares). México: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano. 8 pp. [With three sister readers of the same date and authorship: Nduu ina nchute ña'a xi ndikutu (also downloaded and read), Nasa ta'an che'en io xi, Sa ta'an een tsa kua'an yuku idu - SIL archives 58825/58826/58831/58832.]
sources.note: Nothing: counting lesson (een ndikutu, uvi ina, uni kolo, kumi nchuxi, o'on ndido'o) and a short story in a practical orthography with apostrophe for glottal stop and no tone or accent marks; the only metalinguistic text is 'El objetivo de este folleto es dar practica a los alumnos para que aprendan a contar los números que es del uno al cinco en su propia lengua materma.' Value: documents that SIL linguist Inga McKendry advised Apoala literacy work in 1999 (a person to ask for unpublished Apoala notes).

sources.citation: Campbell, Michael. [1980, date uncertain]. Procedural Discourse, Story of Wheat Seeds in Apoala. Apoala Mixteco. Typescript, 9 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives 56094 (Bartholomew Collection of Unpublished Materials, SIL Mexico Branch; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). [Companion to A's work 2; the Expository Discourse ms. 56223 (3 pp.) was downloaded and read the same way; the Hortatory ms. 56224 could not be downloaded.]
sources.note: Nothing explicit. 53 interlinear sentences (Mixtec / English word gloss / free translation) organised by discourse slots, then (p. 7) 'As in hortatory discourse there are some rules that seem to be valid for procedural discourse..' with five rules about the connectives sâ 'and', tucu 'also', dana 'then', followed by a paragraph/sentence/ground/figure chart. No transcription key: vowels carry acute and circumflex marks (cuâ 'the', nridâ 'all', xî'î 'with') that are never explained, so pitch is marked impressionistically but not described; the words 'tone', 'stress' and 'accent' occur in neithe…

sources.citation: Bradley, C. Henry & J. Kathryn Josserand (dirs.), CIS-INAH Programa de Lingüística, Proyecto Mixteco. 1977-1979. 'Reconocimiento del mixteco' / 'Cuestionario de sintaxis' dialect-survey questionnaires (ca. 170 towns), ms. transcriptions with tone/stress marks. Archived as 'Mixtec Languages Collection of Kathryn Josserand' (AILLA, UT Austin); crowd-transcribed as 'The Kathryn Josserand Mixtec Language Surveys' (FromThePage, UT Libraries).
sources.note: marks only (already harvested by an earlier reading): phonetic transcription with occasional tone remarks on single items, e.g. X-5 v3 item 'čye n¢atu biko (nube) (tono + bajo)'; no statement.

sources.citation: Jordán, Lorenzo & Raúl García Alvarado. 1968. Letra Tõ'õ Dadavi. En el idioma mixteco de Santiago Apoala (Nochixtlán, Oaxaca) y en español. México, D.F.: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano en coordinación con la Dirección General de Asuntos Indígenas, SEP. (8-021, M51.) 58 [64] pp.
sources.note: Picture alphabet (one keyword per letter, pp. 3-57) plus 'Propósitos' (p. 4) and 'Aclaraciones' (book p. 58): letters shared with Spanish; b g k p w only in loans; 'i' before consonants; 'x' = classical Nahuatl x; 'El apóstrofo representa un saltillo o una ligera oclusión de la garganta entre dos vocales o sílabas, como en las palabras ve'e "casa" y sa'a "pie"'; 'nd' pronounced simultaneously (nda'a 'mano'). No mention of tone (tono) or stress (acento) anywhere; keywords are written without tone or accent marks (only ü/õ diacritics for vowel quality/nasality).
